title: "The Elephant Clock", folio from a Book of the Knowledge of Ingenious Mechanical Devices by al-Jazari
maker: Farrukh ibn `Abd al-Latif (painter), for a copy of the treatise of Badi' al-Zaman ibn al-Razzaz al-Jazari (1206)
medium: Ink, opaque watercolor, and gold on paper
source: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Open Access (CC0), 57.51.23, Bequest of Cora Timken Burnett, 1956
note: Cut off its mount; moving parts (scribe, serpent, bird, balcony man, the mahout's two arms, the cymbal) cut along the painter's ink lines; what they covered restored from the folio's own pixels (the pillar's own shaft, the coil carried round in polar coordinates, the folio's bare paper for fibre and tone). Scaled to 1600 px. Other views of the folio (DT459, ISL151, 57.51.23, is57.51.23.R: earlier photographs before conservation) were compared; DP234075 is the sharpest and the only one used.

title: "Design for the Water Clock of the Peacocks", from the same manuscript
source: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Open Access (CC0), 55.121.15, Rogers Fund, 1955
note: The gold disc painted on the pipe at the right (centre about 2056, 2023 px, radius 101), cut out as a circle and scaled to the size of the falcon's beak: the clock's bronze balls, in this painter's gold.

files: assets/parts.webp (the clean patches: paper fibre and mottle)
title: Sister folios of the same manuscript: paper grain for the restoration, and references
source: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Open Access (CC0)
note: 55.121.13 (the mahout, with the pivots of his arms and the spoon: where the axe arm's axle goes; its bare left and right margins, DP351397 x150-470/2350-2700, y1350-2650, give paper grain) and 55.121.15 (the Peacocks, DP369551 x2300-2640, y2600-3500, paper grain); 55.121.14, 55.121.12, 55.121.11 compared for the ink, the gold and the paper. Grain is high-passed and contrast-matched; only its texture is used.

title: The mechanism
source: Ibn al-Razzaz al-Jazari, The Book of Knowledge of Ingenious Mechanical Devices, translated and annotated by Donald R. Hill (Dordrecht: D. Reidel, 1974), Category I, chapter 4 (the elephant water-clock, 15 sections)
note: Every pivot, the order of events and the setting of the clock (sec. 15) follow this text.
